The main takeaway from our work is that

the present constraints on the supersymmetry parameters are not yet strong enough to make a definitive statement on the size of the CP-violating phases, but the situation is rapidly changing with the new data from the BaBar and Belle experiments.

, while the supersymmetric effects in $\Delta M_s$, $\Delta M_d$ and $\vert\epsilon \vert$ may be comparable to the standard model contributions, the effects in the CP-violating phases are expected to be much smaller, and hence, the CP asymmetries may be dominated by standard model effects.
